subject.title: [Feature]: Support plugin-requestable session isolation for trust boundaries

question: Should OpenClaw expose plugin-requestable quarantined execution as a public Plugin SDK/runtime security-boundary contract, and what guarantees must that contract make?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but it would define a public plugin API and a security boundary; automation should not choose the enforcement semantics, trust metadata shape, or compatibility expectations.

options.title: Keep As Design Item
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers define isolation semantics, trust metadata, prerequisite hook context, and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Document Current Primitives
options.body: Document sessions_spawn with sandbox=require, per-agent tool policy, and separate gateway or OS boundaries as the supported workaround without adding a hook directive yet.

options.title: Reject Plugin-Requested Quarantine
options.body: Close the direction if maintainers decide strong isolation must remain at separate gateway, OS user, host, or operator-managed sandbox boundaries only.

recommendation.title: Keep As Design Item
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers define isolation semantics, trust metadata, prerequisite hook context, and compatibility expectations.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on subagent sandboxing and control-boundary hardening, which are central to the proposed contract.
